I am 72, and I have farmed for a long time, so I will keep this year simple, steady, and manageable with the labor my household has. I have only 2 people at home, so I will not spread myself too thin or take on high-risk changes. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on wheat and maize as the main part of my land since that wheat-maize system is what I know best and it gives me stable grain. I will keep part of the farm in cotton because I already grow it and I do not want to abandon it, but I will not put too much land into it because cotton needs more field watching and more pesticide work. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps me get stable emergence and yield, and I will keep fertilizer at moderate levels because I want dependable production, not the highest possible input. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing on all land. With irrigation from the well, I will water wheat more than the other crops, give maize key irrigations in summer, and give cotton a few irrigations when it needs them. I will also keep pesticide sprays moderate: fewer on wheat, more on maize and especially cotton, because that matches the problems I usually expect in the field.
